The '''EE-3 carbine rifle''' was a blaster that was modeled after the [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]] later used by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. The rifle consisted of a small handle attached to a long circular [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]]. At least two versions of the EE-3 were known to exist, with one featuring a hand grip covering the length of the barrel.

==History==
[[File:Counter_Stroke_TCG_Baracchi.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] slices Boba Fett's EE-3 in half with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].]]

The [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Sugi (bounty hunter)/Legends|Sugi]] wielded an EE-3 during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. [[Kiera Swan/Legends|Kiera Swan]] used this weapon in the [[Box/Legends|Box]]. The EE-3 was also the standard-issue weapon for the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]].

The [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] almost exclusively used the EE-3 as his primary weapon. Fett modified his by adding a [[Stock/Legends|stock]] and an electronic scope for distance shooting, making it a dangerous weapon. [[Xizor/Legends|Prince Xizor]] also used an EE-3 to try to kill [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] as the Jedi and his friends escaped the [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen's]] palace on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

{{Weapon-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the rifle discharges a three-round burst. In the game, Fett's blaster uses the same model as the E-11 Blaster Rifle.

The prop Boba Fett uses in the films is a modified Webley & Scott № 1 Mark "I" Flare Gun, built for use by British troops during WWI. To make it into the weapon of an intergalactic bounty hunter, prop makers added a rifle scope, some detail parts to the stock and either an MPP Microflash or Heiland Synchronar flash unit protruding from the end of the barrel. There were also some blocky detail pieces added between the scope mounts and the body of the gun.

[[File:Sugi_EE-3.png|thumb|right|200px|Sugi's use of a EE-3 in ''The Clone Wars'']]
In [[2010]], [[Bounty Hunters (episode)|''Bounty Hunters'']], an episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, showed a bounty hunter wielding an EE-3. The EE-3 later reappeared in the show in the episode ''[[The Box]]'' and again in [[Eminence (episode)|''Eminence'']].

The barrel of the gun was chopped off by a [[Subject 1138|clone]] of [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] in [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''The Force Unleashed II'' novel]].

In {{Film|VI}}, the Webley & Scott was used again, only this time more detail was added, primarily to the barrel. Presumably this was because the prop would be featured prominently in the skiff battle scenes where Luke Skywalker slices it in half with his lightsaber. The Heiland flash unit was gone and a beefier barrel with ribbed hand grips was built ''over'' the existing flare gun barrel. The same scope was used, but it was mounted pointing in the opposite direction from the {{Film|V}} version. The scope was also mounted farther back on the gun and slightly lower. The blocky detail parts on the scope mounts were also eliminated.
